uncataloged.reason: Verified against internal/acdsl/policy.go: CheckPolicy's baseErr branch (if baseErr != nil { if policy.Mode == PolicyModeFree { return nil, nil } ... }) checks the raw, untrusted working-tree policy.Mode directly, before basePolicy() ever loads the authoritative base-committed policy - contradicting the function's own doc comment ("The base-ref policy is authoritative - a branch cannot weaken the mode by editing... the working policy only bootstraps base resolution"). Setting policy.BaseRef also fully replaces the origin/HEAD->origin/main->main->master fallback candidates with just that one ref (candidates = []string{policy.BaseRef}), so an attacker can force baseErr on demand even when a legitimate base is reachable. This is a distinct mechanism from the three already-cataloged base-resolution bypasses (GV3-001: pre-policy-base free fallback inside basePolicy; GV3-002: base_ref==own-branch isBoundary spoof; GV4-202: base_ref==HEAD vacuous-diff trick) - none of which touch the baseErr path. GV3-108 also names 'CheckPolicy free+unresolvable-base' but only as an untested-branch (tests/INFO) coverage note, not as a claimed security exploit; it asserts no defect in the behavior itself, so it is a different finding, not a duplicate. Genuine in-range defect, not cataloged as a security/correctness issue anywhere in golden.
